before.question: Which principle best characterizes oral fasting window?
choices: Lefamulin tablets are taken at least one hour before a meal or two hours after a meal
Each IV dose is infused over 60 minutes and the rate should not be exceeded
Strong CYP3A or P-gp inhibitors markedly increase oral lefamulin exposure

Definitive reassessment determines whether the adult still has a supported CABP syndrome, is responding, remains free of an uncovered pathogen or complication, and can safely continue the current route
before.rationale: Food reduces oral exposure and the label requires fasting administration

after.question: Which principle best characterizes oral fasting window?
choices: Lefamulin tablets are taken at least one hour before a meal or two hours after a meal
The meal interval is reversed: take the tablet two hours before or one hour after a meal
Take the tablet with a meal whenever nausea occurs
Only the morning dose requires a fasting window
after.rationale: Each oral dose uses the labeled interval of at least one hour before or two hours after a meal. Reversing those intervals, routinely taking the dose with food, or exempting the evening dose does not follow the label. The single-dose high-fat, high-calorie meal study found lower peak concentration and overall exposure; it does not measure a universal effect for every meal or enteral-feed regimen.

before.question: Which clinical action best applies to oral fasting window?
choices: Build dose times around meals before discharge

before.rationale: Food reduces oral exposure and the label requires fasting administration

after.question: Which clinical action best applies to oral fasting window?
choices: Build dose times around meals before discharge
Choose convenient dose times first and ask the patient to fit meals around them later
Give both daily tablets at breakfast to avoid two fasting windows

after.rationale: Plan the twice-daily dose times and labeled meal intervals together before discharge. Deferring that planning can leave an impractical schedule, combining both tablets is not every-12-hour dosing, and taking each dose with food conflicts with the oral instructions. Nausea warrants assessment without automatically replacing the fasting rule.

before.question: Which principle best characterizes missed dose rule?
choices: A missed dose may be taken only when at least eight hours remain before the next scheduled dose

after.question: Which principle best characterizes missed dose rule?
choices: A missed dose may be taken only when at least eight hours remain before the next scheduled dose
A missed dose should be taken whenever at least six hours remain before the next dose

after.rationale: Take a missed dose as soon as possible if at least eight hours remain before the next scheduled dose. Six hours is below the cutoff; twelve hours is not the required threshold. This is the labeled scheduling rule, not a measured concentration calculation.

after.question: Which principle best characterizes oral adherence design?
choices: Every oral course requires alignment of twice-daily timing, fasting windows, whole-tablet swallowing, and interaction avoidance

teachingReview.before: Take a missed dose when at least eight hours remain before the next scheduled dose. If fewer than eight hours remain, skip it and resume the schedule.

teachingReview.heading: A short course can still be operationally difficult
teachingReview.before: Twice-daily fasting windows, whole-tablet swallowing, interactions, cost, and access can defeat adherence. Test the schedule with the patient before discharge.
teachingReview.after: Twice-daily fasting windows, whole-tablet swallowing, interactions, cost, and access can defeat adherence. Test the schedule with the patient before discharge. The labeled initial oral adult CABP course is 600 mg every 12 hours for five days. Confirm that the patient can obtain and complete it, apply the meal and missed-dose instructions, and communicate medication changes. An IV-to-oral switch completes its planned treatment course rather than automatically starting a new five-day course.

after.question: A patient remembers a dose with six hours before the next scheduled tablet. What should happen?
choices: Skip the missed dose and resume the next scheduled dose
Take two tablets immediately
Take the missed tablet with a meal
Restart the five-day count
after.rationale: Six hours is below the eight-hour cutoff. Skip the missed tablet and resume at the next scheduled time; do not take two tablets, take the ineligible missed tablet with a meal, or automatically restart a five-day course.

after.question: Which principle best characterizes oral adherence design?
choices: Every oral course requires alignment of twice-daily timing, fasting windows, whole-tablet swallowing, and interaction avoidance
A five-day course makes meal timing unnecessary
Keeping tablets intact removes the need to review interacting medications
Once the daily milligram total is correct, both tablets can be taken together
after.rationale: The labeled oral course combines every-12-hour timing, fasting intervals, intact-tablet swallowing and medication-interaction review. Five days does not waive meal rules, intact tablets do not neutralize CYP or QT interactions, and matching daily milligrams does not authorize combining the doses. Build a plan the patient can actually follow.
